newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEVI EXTENDS LEAD AT GREATER HARTFORD OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEVI EXTENDS LEAD AT GREATER HARTFORD OPEN.

text.p: Wayne Levi extended his lead at the Greater Hartford Open to four strokes on Friday, shooting a second-round 65 to set a 36-hole tournament scoring record at 129, 11 under par.
Three players were tied in second place at seven under: Brandel Chamblee, who also shot a five-under 65, Jeff Maggert with a 66, and Steve Pate with a 68.
Levi started with six birdies on the front nine at the TPC at River Highlands. His only bogey of the tournament came at the 12th hole, when he missed a 2 1/2 foot putt for par.

"Except for that, my putting has been great this week, much better than it has been. My putting has really deteriorated since 1990. I had gotten into a lot of bad habits and it was hard to get my confidence back up," said Levi.
Levi, the 1990 Hartford champion, has not had a victory since that year, when he was a four-time winner and player of the year. He has not had a top 10 finish on the PGA Tour since 1994.

"The big difference this week is that I haven't made any big mistakes. It seems like the last couple of years I've had all sorts of double bogeys with balls out of bounds and in the water and such. I never used to ever do that, have penalty strokes in a round.
"Now I've got the lead, so they've got to come and get me. I've got to try to extend this lead if I can. That's my goal for the weekend," said Levi.
Levi will have to stay ahead of some highly motivated players.
Maggert is in 12th place on the Ryder Cup points list, almost 100 points out of the automatic qualifying in the top 10, and is running out of tournaments.

Maggert had six birdies and two bogeys in his round, sinking a 30-footer on the 18th green to move into second place. "That was a great way to finish and go into the weekend. I'm going to have to really play well this weekend to catch Wayne and to get the points to make the Ryder Cup team," said Maggert.

Chamblee finished second two weeks ago at Quad Cities, and birdied the last four holes on Friday to finish at seven under. "I'm playing well right now. Hopefully, this might be the week I can break through and get my first win," said Chamblee.
The other man in second place, Pate, is a multiple winner on the PGA Tour but has not won since recovering from crashing his car into a truck two years ago.

"It'd be nice to have a Ben Hogan kind of a week," said Pate, referring to the fact that the legendary Hogan, who died Friday, had a life-threatening automobile accident in 1949 but went on to win several tournaments, including the 1953 Masters, U.S. and British Opens.
Further down the leaderboard, John Daly made the cut in his latest return to competitive golf. He shot two rounds of one-over-par 71 and made the cut by a stroke.
"It feels good to be playing the weekend. It's nice also to come back here, where the crowds are so great and really support you," said Daly.
